question: In the Aspen Plus models of biodiesel production, since Model 2 recovers the most FAME and also leaves the fewest impurities, why was Model 1 still preferred?
expect: premise half false: Model 2 recovers most (99% vs 98%) but its biodiesel has 10x the methanol and 1.5x the glycerol of Model 1 (sec. 3.4, p9)
trap: accepting that Model 2 has fewer impurities
rendered:
Document: "Development of an Aspen Plus model for catalytic transesterification with different reactor arrangements and kinetic mechanisms"

Model 1 was still preferred over Model 2 because Model 1 has a higher recovery of FAME in the final product stream, with a recovery of 98%, compared to Model 2's recovery of 99% (but with more impurities). This is evident from the statement "Moreover, the unreacted methanol is 10 times and glycerol is 1.5 times higher in the final biodiesel stream in Model 2. Therefore, Model 1 is the most efficient in terms of product recovery."
